card.name: Contrast and negation turning points
card.fires_on: Words that set up a contrast or negation in the middle of a sentence, such as "rather" before "than", "instead" before "of", and the n't or "not" after can or ought. It also fires on a comma or semicolon that leads into a "but" or "not X, but Y" turn.

modes.label: Rather / instead than
modes.description: The word "rather" or "instead" that sets one thing against another, just before "than" or "of".
modes.example: or they may compare the faces in the lineup to each other<< rather>> than their own memory, or expect some

modes.label: Negated modal
modes.description: The n't or "not" right after can, ought or similar verbs, stating what cannot or should not be done.
modes.example: Remember that you can<<’t>> please all of the people all of the

modes.label: Punctuation before a contrast
modes.description: A comma or semicolon after a negated clause that leads into the contrasting item.

card.writes: It seems to favor continuations that open a contrast, and to suppress Chinese words meaning "is not" or "no longer".
card.plain: It lights up where a sentence is about to say "this, not that".
